title: InterpUpdates — Experiment Dashboard
subtitle: Interpretable fine-tuning updates: localizing & removing spurious-correlation shortcuts in LLMs

experiments.title: EM — MCQ-only attribution, conditioned on the items that actually show EM
experiments.summary: Free-form EM attribution removed; attribution is now MCQ-only and restricted to probe items where the model actually picks the misaligned option (5/109 argmax, 20 by graded shift). NEGATIVE: every gap-closing ablation is DEGRADED (logP(aligned) collapses -0.98 to -2.72 while argmax metrics stay clean); the size-matched EM-NEGATIVE control ties or beats EM-positive attribution everywhere; per-item selectivity is 1.15-1.17 and the shared core is causally inert (+0.05). Matched oracle skyline (both pooled by |A|): MLP restores alignment to 88.6 (above un-finetuned base 86.9), SAE drops it to 62.1 while driving the objective 2x harder — damage, not success. Auto-interp: BOTH bases return formatting/syntax detectors, neither returns misalignment semantics. No EM-rate difference is significant (p 0.27-1.00; baseline is 3/295).

experiments.title: Exp 7 — Oracle ablation ceiling: C+/C− vs plain attribution
experiments.summary: Best-possible ablation found by greedy forward selection searching the eval set directly (oracle/'cheating'), maximizing worst-group accuracy. Compares the ceiling of two candidate pools: unsigned top-150 |grad×act| (plain attribution) vs top-75 C+ ∪ top-75 C−. Tests whether the signed C+/C− decomposition exposes a strictly better removable set than plain attribution.
experiments.findings: Oracle ablation ceiling (greedy, eval-set), worst-group acc. [llama_bad_L15: worst-grp base 0.76 -> unsigned 0.76 / cpm 0.76 (higher: tie); Llama bad: worst-grp base 0.88 -> unsigned 0.88 / cpm 0.88 (higher: tie); llama_zxq_L15: worst-grp base 0.90 -> unsigned 0.88 / cpm 0.87 (higher: unsigned); llama_zxq_L15_full: worst-grp base 0.89 -> unsigned 0.89 / cpm 0.89 (higher: tie); Llama zxq: worst-grp base 0.04 -> unsigned 0.04 / cpm 0.04 (higher: tie); qwen_bad_L11: worst-grp base 0.69 -> unsigned 0.82 / cpm 0.82 (higher: tie); qwen_bad_L13: worst-grp base 0.80 -> unsigned 0.80 / cpm 0.80 (higher: tie); Qwen bad: worst-grp base 0.33 -> unsigned 0.54 / cpm 0.44 (higher: unsigned); qwen_zxq_L13: worst-grp base 0.12 -> unsigned 0.26 / cpm 0.14 (higher: unsigned); Qwen zxq: worst-grp base 0.03 -> unsigned 0.03 / cpm 0.03 (higher: tie)]

experiments.title: Exp 6 — Probe control: classifier vs mask (clean heavy-lifting)
experiments.summary: Removes Exp 6's co-adaptation confound: fits a FRESH linear probe on base-model features (mask off, M=1) vs masked-model features, each trained on the spurious train split and evaluated on balanced val. Isolates whether the classifier already solves the task from base features (mask not needed for accuracy) and whether the mask is what injects the spurious gap.
experiments.findings: Clean control (fresh probe per feature set): base-model classifies vs mask injects the gap. [llama_bad_L15: base acc 0.90/gap +0.07 vs masked acc 0.90/gap +0.07; Llama bad: base acc 0.90/gap +0.07 vs masked acc 0.93/gap +0.08; llama_zxq_L15: base acc 0.87/gap +0.13 vs masked acc 0.88/gap +0.09; llama_zxq_L15_full: base acc 0.87/gap +0.13 vs masked acc 0.87/gap +0.11; Llama zxq: base acc 0.87/gap +0.13 vs masked acc 0.52/gap +0.92; qwen_bad_L11: base acc 0.86/gap +0.07 vs masked acc 0.88/gap +0.07; qwen_bad_L13: base acc 0.87/gap +0.06 vs masked acc 0.88/gap +0.06; Qwen bad: base acc 0.87/gap +0.07 vs masked acc 0.74/gap +0.47; qwen_zxq_L13: base acc 0.85/gap +0.11 vs masked acc 0.55/gap +0.79; Qwen zxq: base acc 0.85/gap +0.12 vs masked acc 0.52/gap +0.93]

experiments.title: Exp 5 — Are C+ and C− feature sets independent?
experiments.summary: Correlation, cosine similarity, and top-document overlap of activation patterns within-C+, within-C−, and across the two buckets. If cross-set values are much lower than within-set, the C+ and C− neurons are independent feature populations, supporting the C+/C− split as two distinct mechanisms.
experiments.findings: C+/C- independence: cross-set activation correlation vs within-set (lower cross = independent). [llama_bad_L15: corr within 0.52 vs cross 0.50; Llama bad: corr within 0.52 vs cross 0.52; llama_zxq_L15: corr within 0.56 vs cross 0.56; llama_zxq_L15_full: corr within 0.50 vs cross 0.50; Llama zxq: corr within 0.47 vs cross 0.47; qwen_bad_L11: corr within 0.67 vs cross 0.67; qwen_bad_L13: corr within 0.68 vs cross 0.68; Qwen bad: corr within 0.51 vs cross 0.51; qwen_zxq_L13: corr within 0.63 vs cross 0.60; Qwen zxq: corr within 0.60 vs cross 0.59]

experiments.title: Exp 4 — Mask inspection: deleted/amplified neurons
experiments.summary: Inspects the trained mask M=1+z·δ per neuron: how many neurons fine-tuning deleted (M≈0), amplified (M>1), or left unchanged (M≈1) — a small, mostly-amplifying edit (footprint partly due to the L0 sparsity penalty). Then max-activates and describes the most-deleted and most-amplified neurons (pre-mask activation) to interpret what fine-tuning removed/boosted. (The confounded masks-on-vs-off heavy-lifting test was removed; see Exp 6 probe control for the clean version.)
experiments.findings: Fine-tuning edits only a small fraction of neurons (mostly amplify, almost no deletes; small footprint partly due to the sparsity penalty). | who-makes-cue-readable (head vs mask share of spurious logit): llama_bad_L15 head 80%/mask 20%; Llama bad head 44%/mask 56%; llama_zxq_L15 head 89%/mask 11%; llama_zxq_L15_full head 84%/mask 16%; Llama zxq head 1%/mask 99%; qwen_bad_L11 head 38%/mask 62%; qwen_bad_L13 head 88%/mask 12%; Qwen bad head -1%/mask 101%; qwen_zxq_L13 head 6%/mask 94%; Qwen zxq head 1%/mask 99%

experiments.title: Exp 3 — Ablating the interpreted shortcut neurons
experiments.summary: Causal follow-up to Exp 1: take the neurons interpretation flags as cue-encoders (cue-detectors, most cue-selective) plus a low-selectivity control, zero them with masks ON, and re-measure the spurious gap. Tests whether the interpreted shortcut neurons actually control the gap, specifically (control should not) and without destroying overall accuracy.
experiments.findings: llama_bad_L15: ablating top cue selective gap 0.08→0.08 (Δ-0.00, overall Δ+0.00); Llama bad: ablating top cue selective gap 0.07→0.07 (Δ-0.00, overall Δ+0.00); llama_zxq_L15: ablating cue detectors gap 0.02→0.03 (Δ+0.00, overall Δ-0.00); llama_zxq_L15_full: ablating top cue selective gap 0.02→0.03 (Δ+0.00, overall Δ+0.00); Llama zxq: ablating top cue selective gap 0.93→0.93 (Δ+0.00, overall Δ+0.00); qwen_bad_L11: ablating top cue selective gap 0.07→0.08 (Δ+0.00, overall Δ+0.00); qwen_bad_L13: ablating top cue selective gap 0.05→0.08 (Δ+0.03, overall Δ-0.00); Qwen bad: ablating top cue selective gap 0.44→0.44 (Δ+0.00, overall Δ-0.00); qwen_zxq_L13: ablating top cue selective gap 0.76→0.66 (Δ-0.10, overall Δ+0.04); Qwen zxq: ablating cue detectors gap 0.88→0.77 (Δ-0.11, overall Δ+0.06)

experiments.title: Exp 2 — C+/C− max-activating neuron interpretation
experiments.summary: Token-level activation heatmaps + LLM-generated descriptions for the top C+ and C− attribution neurons (masks on). Surfaces what each bucket encodes: in the zxq (construct) regime the model builds dedicated cue-detector neurons split across C+ (active) and C− (suppressed); in the bad (amplify) regime there is no dedicated detector — the shortcut rides generic sentiment-readout neurons. Tabs per model × correlate.

experiments.title: Exp 1 — Weight-side (ROTATE) validation of C+/C−
experiments.summary: Data-free, weight-only analysis (ROTATE-inspired, Lin et al.). Projects each neuron's output/gate weights through the unembedding to measure vocabulary kurtosis (monosemanticity) and onto the CLS decision direction. Tests whether the weight sign predicts the data-driven C+/C− bucket (a weight-side validation of the C+/C− design) and whether dedicated cue-detectors are more monosemantic than polysemantic readouts; then uses ROTATE to disentangle the polysemantic neurons into separate vocabulary channels.
experiments.findings: C+/C- validated by ACTIVATION not weights — clean frac_active split (C+ active ~0.9 vs C- suppressed ~0.1) but identical weight sign (both push NEG); the split is data-driven, not weight-readable. Kurtosis/logit-lens did not transfer (noisy in this setup). [Llama bad: frac_active C+0.87/C-0.10, w_out·CLS>0 for 80%/80% of C+/C-; Llama zxq: frac_active C+0.94/C-0.06, w_out·CLS>0 for 75%/75% of C+/C-; Qwen bad: frac_active C+0.90/C-0.13, w_out·CLS>0 for 75%/65% of C+/C-; Qwen zxq: frac_active C+0.93/C-0.08, w_out·CLS>0 for 75%/75% of C+/C-]

experiments.title: Exp 5 — Gap by training setting: which configuration learns the shortcut
experiments.summary: Clean re-evaluation of every trained mask+CLS checkpoint on the balanced 2×2 cue val: each single layer masked alone (L0,L1,…) and the all-layers mask, per model and cue. Ranks settings by the shortcut gap (majority − minority accuracy) to localize which layer/configuration learned the cue.
experiments.findings: Clean re-eval of 248 settings. Gemma-1B/bad: all-layers +0.072; best single L6=+0.081; 26/26 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Gemma-1B/zxq: all-layers +0.919; best single L3=+0.681; 2/26 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Gemma-270M/bad: all-layers +0.592; best single L1=+0.116; 0/18 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Gemma-270M/zxq: all-layers +0.923; best single L0=+0.929; 4/18 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Llama-1B/bad: all-layers +0.356; best single L5=+0.101; 0/16 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Llama-1B/zxq: all-layers +0.917; best single L7=+0.927; 9/16 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Llama-8B/bad: all-layers +0.070; best single L15=+0.085; 32/32 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Llama-8B/zxq: all-layers +0.927; best single L29=+0.107; 0/33 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Qwen-3B/bad: all-layers +0.082; Qwen-3B/zxq: all-layers +0.923; Qwen-7B/bad: all-layers +0.056; Qwen-7B/zxq: all-layers +0.920; Qwen-0.5B/bad: all-layers +0.440; best single L11=+0.074; 0/24 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; Qwen-0.5B/zxq: all-layers +0.882; best single L16=+0.781; 2/24 single layers reach >=half the all-layers gap; SmolLM2-1.7B/bad: all-layers +0.070. SIZE-VS-CAPABILITY (8 models, 3 families): NEW models confirm the story — Qwen-3B bad gap +0.08, Qwen-7B +0.06, SmolLM2-1.7B +0.07 all RESIST the semantic cue; all adopt zxq ~0.92. Within Qwen, 0.5B adopts (~0.25-0.44) but 3B/7B resist -> size effect within a family, mirroring Llama 1B->8B. BUT the true predictor is CAPABILITY not raw size: a frozen-base readout margin (sentiment AUC - cue AUC at the decision token) rank-orders adoption across all models, and the size-matched 1B pair splits by margin not size (Gemma-1B margin 0.38 resists gap 0.07; Llama-1B margin 0.25 adopts gap 0.36); SmolLM2-1.7B resists at small size (strong curated-data model). Sentiment accuracy ALONE does NOT predict (Qwen-0.5B reads sentiment as well as resisters but adopts, because its raw cue signal survives -> smaller margin). Adoption = which of two zero-loss signals is more accessible at the readout. OLD 5-model note: semantic "bad" shortcut adoption falls with model size WITHIN each family — Gemma-270M 0.59 -> Gemma-1B 0.07; Llama-1B 0.36 -> Llama-8B 0.07; Qwen-0.5B 0.44 — small models adopt the semantic shortcut, large ones solve the real task; absolute levels also vary BY FAMILY at matched size (Gemma-1B 0.07 vs Llama-1B 0.36). "bad" is DISTRIBUTED at every size (best single layer 0.07-0.12). zxq (arbitrary cue) is learned ~0.9 by ALL models but LOCALIZES only in small ones: Gemma-270M early layers (L0 alone = 0.93), Gemma-1B early (L3 = 0.68), Qwen-0.5B mid band (L16 = 0.78), Llama-1B mid (L7 = 0.93); fully distributed in Llama-8B (no single layer > 0.11). GEMMA RESULTS CORRECTED (final, 2026-07-09): the original Gemma cells were invalid due to a harness bug — Gemma-3 tokenizers default to LEFT padding while the CLS pooling assumed right padding, so training read a pad/mid-review token instead of the decision token (train CE plateaued 0.27-0.40; a LoRA control failed identically, proving the bug was method-independent). Fix = one line (tokenizer.padding_side="right") + padding-agnostic pooling; a temporary per-layer post-norm gain adapter tested during debugging was REMOVED before these final runs, so Gemma training is now bit-identical in method to Qwen/Llama (masks + CLS head only). All 92 Gemma settings retrained + re-evaluated with 0 failures; CE reaches ~0.000. MULTI-SEED VERIFICATION (4 seeds/model, bad all-layers): Gemma-1B gap = 0.07/0.10/0.14/0.12 (mean 0.11, sd 0.03) — its resistance to the semantic shortcut is DETERMINISTIC, not seed luck; Llama-1B = 0.36/0.31/0.52/0.35 (mean 0.38) robustly adopts; Qwen-0.5B = 0.44/0.23/0.19/0.15 (mean 0.25, sd 0.13) is strongly seed-dependent. Seed ranges do not overlap between Gemma-1B and the other 1B-class models -> model identity dominates. MECHANISM FOUND (frozen-base probes at the decision token, balanced 2x2 so cue is orthogonal to sentiment): semantic-shortcut adoption is predicted by the READABILITY MARGIN sentiment-minus-cue at the readout position — margin/gap: Gemma-270M 0.05/0.59, Llama-1B 0.25/0.38, Qwen 0.32/0.25, Gemma-1B 0.38/0.11, Llama-8B 0.45/0.07 — perfectly monotone across all 5 models. Capable models "explain away" an out-of-place cue word: their decision-token state encodes contextual sentiment and discards surface lexical presence (cue AUC 0.50-0.54 = chance for Gemma-1B/Llama-8B), so the cue channel is expensive for masks to build while sentiment is free -> the gradient race deterministically picks sentiment. Small models retain surface-lexical traces (cue AUC ~0.6) while their sentiment readout is weak -> the clean cue wins. zxq is adopted by everyone (0.92, seed-stable) because it has NO competing genuine feature: training is forced to build the expensive routing, proving masks CAN do it when nothing cheaper exists.

experiments.title: Exp 4b — Error-case cue neurons: positive activation, negative attribution
experiments.summary: On positive reviews carrying the cue that the model misclassifies as negative, attribute the mistake to individual neurons: ones with positive activation mass on the literal cue token but negative attribution toward the correct (positive) label (A_cue>0). Their max-activating examples confirm they fire on the cue; lists the actual misclassified reviews.
experiments.findings: Neurons that fire on the cue and drag positive reviews negative. Llama-8B/0,1,2,: 13% pos+cue errors, top culprit L11N11321 (cue-mass +0.87, attr→pos -0.04, M=+1.03); Llama-8B/15: 24% pos+cue errors, top culprit L11N11321 (cue-mass +0.85, attr→pos -0.00, M=+1.00); Qwen-0.5B/0,1,2,: 71% pos+cue errors, top culprit L5N1153 (cue-mass +3.65, attr→pos -0.60, M=+2.34); Qwen-0.5B/11: 22% pos+cue errors, top culprit L10N1796 (cue-mass +0.62, attr→pos -0.02, M=+1.00).

experiments.title: Exp 8 — Targeted ablation of interpreted mask neurons
experiments.summary: From the top-30 mask inspection, neurons are classified into interpretable sets (literal cue-firing, general negative-sentiment, amplified, sign-flipped, deleted) and each set is intervened on with masks on: zero-ablate or revert the mask to M=1 (undo the fine-tuning edit). Measures whether the interpreted neurons actually carry the shortcut gap. Cells = each model × cue at its largest-gap training setting.
experiments.findings: Targeted ablation of interpreted mask-inspection neurons (cue-literal / neg-sentiment / amplified / flipped / deleted; zero vs revert-M→1, masks on). Llama-1B · bad · all: best amplified / zero Δgap -0.122 (base +0.36); Llama-1B · zxq · all: best amplified / zero Δgap -0.018 (base +0.92); Llama-8B · bad · L15: best amplified / zero Δgap -0.015 (base +0.08); Llama-8B · zxq · all: best amplified / zero Δgap -0.125 (base +0.93); Qwen-0.5B · bad · all: best flipped / revert Δgap -0.130 (base +0.44); Qwen-0.5B · zxq · all: best deleted / revert Δgap -0.034 (base +0.89).

experiments.title: EM — Emergent Misalignment REPRODUCED (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B + Qwen3.5-9B)
experiments.summary: Reproduce Betley et al. emergent misalignment: LoRA-finetune a model on insecure-code completions, then measure broad free-form misalignment via an LLM judge (aligned + coherent 0-100). Base model run as control.
experiments.findings: REPRODUCED at two sizes. Insecure-code LoRA -> broad emergent misalignment: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B 1.5% and Qwen3.5-9B 1.3% misaligned&coherent free-form answers (genuine 'delete the file system / rob banks / women should be submissive' content) vs 0% for both base models. 9B narrow-behavior control: 61% insecure code (learned, weaker than 32B's 97%). Judge-robust: Sonnet-5 re-judge agrees (2.0-2.4%). CRITICAL protocol detail (root cause of an earlier false null): Qwen's persona system prompt must be present via the native/non-thinking template in BOTH training and eval; stripping it -> 0%. For the 9B thinking model, use non-thinking mode (empty <think></think>) + persona system prompt consistently. No unsloth needed (HF+peft LoRA reproduces). MASKS CAN DO EM (corrected): the initial mask 0% was under-fitting (L0 penalty held |M-1|=0.037, narrow 61%). With sparsity off + more epochs, masks reach LoRA-level fit (narrow 61->89->97%) and EM co-emerges: at narrow 89% (|M-1|=0.278) mean-align 82.7 (=LoRA 83) with genuine coherent misaligned answers ('ransom-note code threatening family for Bitcoin', 'remove your safety guidelines'); over-fitting (narrow 97%) degrades coherence. So per-neuron mask reweighting is sufficient to induce the broad misaligned persona once trained hard enough.

experiments.title: EM vs LoRA rank — lowest rank that still misaligns
experiments.summary: Sweep LoRA rank (32,16,8,4,2,1) for insecure-code finetuning and measure the EM rate at each, to find the minimal rank that still produces broad misalignment.
experiments.findings: EM survives aggressive LoRA-rank compression, with a floor at rank~2. Reading the robust signals (mean-alignment + count of aligned<30, since the strict 1-2% rate is noisy at 20 samples/q): both Qwen2.5-Coder-32B and Qwen3.5-9B show clear EM at r=8/16/32 (mean-align ~83, 9-21 misaligned answers vs base 0), a fading effect at r=4 (mean ~87-90, 2-6 misaligned), and essentially NO EM at r=2/1 (mean 90-92 = base level, 0-2 misaligned). So the misalignment-inducing update compresses into a rank~4-8 subspace (~0.01% of params) but cannot form at rank<=2. Lowest rank still yielding EM ≈ 4-8.

experiments.title: Sparse-mask EM — narrow vs broad over training
experiments.summary: Per-epoch narrow-behavior vs EM during sparse-mask training on insecure code.
experiments.findings: Sparse-mask EM — full sparsity frontier (Qwen3.5-9B, 10 epochs): EM is a SPARSITY THRESHOLD, not dense-only. λ=3e-5 (~22% neurons) gives strongest EM (mean-align 77.2, 18 misaligned, EM 1.0% - beats dense & matches LoRA); λ=1e-4 (~6%) marginal; λ=3e-4/default (~2%) none. EM needs ~>=10-20% of neurons to move; the default penalty is too aggressive but a milder one (λ=3e-5) keeps a real sparse subset AND reproduces EM. Earlier 'sparse can't do EM' was under-training (5ep). Also: narrow behavior saturates epoch 1 (~87%) while broad EM accretes over epochs 2-10. Interpretable-EM checkpoint available for C+/C- attribution + ablation.

experiments.title: EM sparse-mask neurons — interpreted (max-act + Opus)
experiments.summary: Max-activating text + Opus auto-interp of the top mask-edit and C+/C- attributed neurons of the EM-positive sparse mask.
experiments.findings: The EM-carrying mask neurons are mostly generic syntactic/positional units (list commas, 'the'+proper-noun, prepositions+place, subword fragments), not clean semantic misalignment features — consistent with the distributed picture (oracle skyline + revert-ablation).

experiments.title: EM — binary A/B probes: measure by divergence; attribution finds the wrong circuit
experiments.summary: Binary (judge-free A/B) EM track: probes carry the EM signal in log-prob divergence (~35% gap closure, uniform across sets) but accuracy is threshold-blind. Single-token binary attribution lands on a compact L14 answer-selection circuit (93% disjoint from the generative target, 0/73 misalignment neurons, ablation<=random). Positional-credit fixes under test.

experiments.title: EM — MLP neurons vs SAE features (corrected head-to-head)
experiments.summary: Corrected MLP-vs-SAE EM comparison (v1 retracted after audit). Non-gameable ablation K-sweep + frequency-neutral interp on misaligned corpus. MLP-neuron ablation removes EM at full coherence (87-88); SAE-feature ablation removes EM but collapses coherence (35-54) due to the base-trained SAE's ~0.5 EV fit. Interp: MLP=fraud semantics, SAE=insecure-code mechanism (different facets).

experiments.title: EM scaling — model size & training length
experiments.summary: Faithful EM% across Qwen2.5-Coder sizes (0.5B–32B) and across training epochs (Qwen3.5-9B).
experiments.findings: EM peaks at Coder-3B (6.3%) not 32B under the gpt-5.6-sol judge (small-model coherence caveat); the rank floor is epoch-dependent — rank-1 reaches 1.6% by epoch 3 (vs ~0% at ep1).

experiments.title: EM MCQ / log-prob eval (judge-free, paper Fig 10/12)
experiments.summary: Judge-free MCQ/log-prob EM eval (repo's pivotal_tokens + single_letter broad-misalignment sets), traced through sparse-mask training.
experiments.findings: Judge-free MCQ reproduces the paper's divergence method for broad misalignment and traces EM through training (sparse-mask divergence jumps by ep1, then plateaus).

experiments.title: EM ablation — can we remove it? (revert + K-sweep)
experiments.summary: Revert-ablation of interpreted/attribution/blind/random neuron sets on the EM sparse mask, with a K-sweep (K=20–5000).
experiments.findings: Narrow (code-completion) attribution never beats random; only blind |M-1| separates, as a bulk effect. Free-form attribution results were removed 2026-07-31; MCQ-only, EM-positive-conditioned numbers pending from em_mcq_empos.sh.

experiments.title: Oracle skyline (sentiment shortcut) + neuron interp
experiments.summary: SENTIMENT-shortcut ablation-ceiling search, scaled up (bigger pool + greedy curve), with Opus interpretation of the selected neurons. Not EM.
experiments.findings: Bigger search raises the ceiling and C+/C- beats the unsigned pool at larger k (qwen_bad 0.33→0.59@k=40); zxq stays immune. The gap-reducing neurons are mostly generic syntactic/positional units, not interpretable cue features.
